pr.title: Stop test chunks with the shared process-group helpers
pr.head: 95ab6b5d654381e2f0c189a560b6ec1993849c50

summary: The parallel test runner divides tests into chunks, with each chunk running in its own worker process. A chunk that hangs must end together with its child processes, or those children can keep the output pipes open and stall the whole run.
This change uses Projector’s existing process-group helpers to start and stop each chunk. Unix keeps the same group cleanup; Windows gains the shared taskkill /T path, which stops a process tree.

The revised head removes the test that counted calls to an internal helper and its unused probe. The existing tests still check timeout cleanup, interrupted cleanup, and closed stdin. The earlier review finding is fixed.

cards.title: Review evidence
cards.html:
• 54 runner, process-helper, and CI tests pass.
  • The configured gate passes, including 270 hook tests and the required CI check.
  • Windows behavior is checked through the shared helper’s mocked regression; a native Windows run was unavailable.

groups.title: Stop each test process tree
groups.kicker: Share process creation and cleanup across platforms
intro: A process group lets the runner stop a worker and its descendants together. The runner now starts chunks with process_group() and stops them with kill_group(), the same helpers used by other Projector commands.

Timeouts, Ctrl-C, and a chunk that starts after interruption all use the shared cleanup path. The tests retain their checks on observable cleanup behavior and remove the internal call-count assertion and its unused probe.

files.note: The parallel test runner starts isolated workers and stops their whole process trees on timeout or interruption.

checks.text: Traced all three cleanup paths to the shared helper and ran the timeout and Ctrl-C regression tests. On Unix, the shared helper sends the same group signal as the removed local helper.

files.note: Runner regressions cover closed stdin, timeout cleanup, interruption cleanup, and the timeout help text.

checks.text: Verified that the internal call-count test and its unused probe are removed. The focused run passes all 54 tests, including the retained timeout and interruption cleanup regressions.
